summary.text: Father of the Halizone captains Odius (`odius-halizone`) and Epistrophus (`epistrophus-halizone`) — attested by Apollodorus among the Trojan allies, while Homer names the sons but not their sire.

story.text: Homer's Catalogue sets Odius and Epistrophus at the head of the Halizones from far-off Alybe, where silver is born — but the poet does not name their father in the muster.

Apollodorus makes Odius and Epistrophus sons of Mecisteus among the Alizones who joined the Trojans. He must be kept distinct from Mecisteus son of Talaus (`mecisteus-aeolid`), from Mecisteus son of Echius (`mecisteus-echius`), and from the Dulichian suitor (`mecisteus-dulichium`).
